style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: De profundis -- 'out of the depths' -- the sixth of the church's seven penitential psalms and Luther's favorite, the one he called a Pauline psalm because the whole gospel is in it. It rises in four steps of two verses each, like the pilgrim road it was sung on. From the depths: a drowning man's cry, asking only that the Lord's ears bend toward him. Then the great question and answer that settle the human condition in two lines: if You, LORD, kept the record of iniquities, who could stand? -- no one; but with You there is forgiveness, and this is the argument no other religion dares -- forgiveness THAT You may be feared, mercy producing reverence, pardon as the foundation of awe. Then the waiting: soul stretched toward the LORD like watchmen on the wall straining for dawn, more than watchmen for the morning -- repeated, because the repetition is what waiting feels like. And finally the arms flung wide to the whole assembly: hope in the LORD, Israel, for with Him is covenant love and redemption in abundance, and He Himself will redeem Israel from all his iniquities -- the psalm's last word answering its first, the depths of sin swallowed by the greater depths of grace.

1.text: A song of ascents. Out of the depths I cry up to You, O LORD.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. Out of the depths [maamaqim -- the deep waters, the drowning places] have I cried [qara] unto You, O LORD [YHWH].
1.notes: maamaqim (H4615) are the deep waters over a drowning man's head (cf. Psalm 69:2) -- here the depths of guilt, the flood of verse 3. The psalm's first motion is the only one available at that depth: qara (H7121), the cry straight up. Prayers from the bottom reach as far as prayers from the mountaintop.

2.text: Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears bend close and attend to the voice of my pleadings for grace.
2.amp: Lord [Adonai], hear [shama] my voice [qol]: let Your ears [ozen] be attentive [qashshab -- listening intently] to the voice of my supplications [tachanun -- pleas for grace].
2.notes: qashshab (H7183) is the leaning ear, attention sharpened to a point. tachanun (H8469) is built on the grace-root chanan: not petitions arguing merit but pleadings for undeserved favor -- the only currency the depths accept.

3.text: If You, O LORD, kept watch over iniquities -- Lord, who could stand?
3.amp: If You, LORD [Yah], should mark [shamar -- keep watch over, keep the record of] iniquities [avon], O Lord [Adonai], who shall stand [amad]?
3.notes: The keeping-verb of Psalm 121 turned to its terrifying alternative: shamar (H8104) applied to avon (H5771), God as record-keeper of guilt. The question mi yaamod (H5975), who could stand, is left hanging because every honest reader answers it the same way (cf. Nahum 1:6; Romans 3:19-20).

4.text: But with You forgiveness is found -- so that You may be feared.
4.amp: But there is forgiveness [selichah -- pardon] with You, that You may be feared [yare -- revered, held in awe].
4.notes: selichah (H5547): pardon lodged WITH God, kept in stock at His house, His alone to give (cf. Daniel 9:9). And the stunning purpose clause: forgiveness in order that He be yare (H3372), feared -- mercy does not shrink reverence, it creates it; the pardoned man fears the LORD as the condemned never could (cf. 1 Kings 8:39-40).

5.text: I wait for the LORD -- my soul waits -- and in His word I have put my hope.
5.amp: I wait [qavah -- wait with the tension of a stretched cord] for the LORD [YHWH], my soul [nephesh] does wait, and in His word [dabar] do I hope [yachal -- wait expectantly].
5.notes: qavah (H6960), the cord-taut waiting of Psalm 27:14, doubled -- I wait, my nephesh waits -- because forgiven men still wait for the full morning of their redemption. The anchor is the dabar (H1697): hope moored to what God has said, not to how the depths feel.

6.text: My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning -- yes, more than watchmen for the morning.
6.amp: My soul [nephesh] waits for the Lord [Adonai] more than they that watch [shamar] for the morning [boqer]: I say, more than they that watch for the morning.
6.notes: The shomrim (H8104) on the night walls: cold, strained, certain that dawn is coming yet aching for it -- waiting that knows the outcome and still counts the minutes. The line repeats because that is what the last watch feels like; and the boqer (H1242) never yet failed a watchman, which is the argument.

7.text: O Israel, hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is covenant love, and with Him is redemption in abundance.
7.amp: Let Israel [Yisrael] hope [yachal] in the LORD [YHWH]: for with the LORD there is mercy [chesed -- covenant love], and with Him is plenteous [rabah -- abundant, multiplied] redemption [peduth].
7.notes: The rescued man turns preacher to the nation: yachal (H3176), hope, commanded corporately. The stock held 'with the LORD' now shows two lines: chesed (H2617) and peduth (H6304), ransom-redemption -- and the inventory word is rabah (H7235), multiplied: more redemption in Him than sin in us (cf. Romans 5:20).

8.text: And He Himself will redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
8.amp: And He shall redeem [padah -- ransom, buy back] Israel [Yisrael] from all [kol] his iniquities [avon].
8.notes: The pronoun is emphatic: He Himself will padah (H6299) -- the Redeemer does the redeeming in person. kol avon: the same word that filled the depths of verse 3, now the object of a completed purchase. The angel's charge to Joseph is this verse with a name attached: 'He shall save His people from their sins' (cf. Matthew 1:21).
